case_title: Thirumoorthy v. State Represented by the Inspector of Police
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.342, s.201 r/w 302, s.363, POCSO Act s.6
confession: Confession recorded in memo (Ex. P-20), relied on by trial court
aggravating_circumstances: Homicidal nature of death, asphyxiation, genital injuries, incised wounds
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to 07 years rigorous imprisonment under s.363 IPC, 01 years under s.342 IPC, 10 years under s.6 POCSO Act, 10 years under s.302 IPC, and 07 years under s.201 r/w 302 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, a juvenile, was involved in the disappearance and subsequent death of a six-year-old girl. The victim's father reported her missing after she failed to return home. The investigating officer identified the accused as a juvenile based on his school records. The accused was apprehended, and a confession was recorded. The victim's body was found concealed in an aluminium vessel. Medical examination confirmed the death was homicidal, caused by asphyxiation and genital injuries. The accused was tried in a Sessions Court designated as a Children’s Court, but the proceedings were later found to have violated the Juvenile Justice Act by not involving the Juvenile Justice Board for preliminary assessment. The trial court proceeded with the trial and sentencing despite the procedural irregularities.
